levels.title: Fundamentals
levels.blurb: LLMs, training, retrieval, tools, memory, the agent loop, and seeing what it did. Start here.

levels.title: Intermediate
levels.blurb: Prompting, context, coding agents and practice with them, harnesses, loops, agentic UI, and security.

levels.title: Expert
levels.blurb: Inside the LLM, fine-tuning and post-training, advanced RAG, tools, memory, multi-agent, prompting, context, coding agents, harnesses, loops, architectures, UI, deployment, agent servers and evaluation.

levels.title: Ecosystem
levels.blurb: Frameworks, inference providers and engines, UI design, and picking a stack.

levels.title: Emerging
levels.blurb: Ideas that are hot in industry and research but not settled yet.

engineers.title: LLM Fundamentals
engineers.summary: What a language model actually does, what the context window costs you, and which knobs change its output.

everyone.title: LLM Fundamentals
everyone.summary: What a language model is, how it reads your chat, and the one limit that shapes everything else in this course.

engineers.title: Training LLMs
engineers.summary: How a general model is born in pre-training, and the two ways you specialise it afterwards.

everyone.title: Training LLMs
everyone.summary: How an empty model learns language from the internet, and how it then learns one skill.

engineers.title: RAG & Embeddings
engineers.summary: Giving a model knowledge it was never trained on, using embeddings and a vector store.

everyone.title: RAG & Embeddings
everyone.summary: How an AI answers from your own documents without being trained on them: find the right pages, then add them to the chat.

engineers.title: Tool Calling
engineers.summary: How a model reaches outside itself, the mechanism underneath every agent.

everyone.title: Tool Calling
everyone.summary: How an AI that can only write text still searches the web, reads files and sends emails: it asks, and a normal program does the work.

engineers.title: Memory
engineers.summary: Three kinds of memory, parametric, working and long-term, and where each one actually lives.

everyone.title: Memory
everyone.summary: An AI remembers nothing by itself. Three kinds of memory, where each one lives, and how a chat only feels continuous.

engineers.title: AI Agents
engineers.summary: The agent loop, and what turns a single model call into multi-step work.

everyone.title: AI Agents
everyone.summary: An AI agent is an LLM in a loop: it uses tools again and again until the job is done. What changes, and what does not.

engineers.title: Multi-Agent Systems
engineers.summary: When one agent stops being enough, the two architectures to know, and the two problems you inherit.

everyone.title: Multi-Agent Systems
everyone.summary: When one agent is not enough: AI agents working as a team, the same way people do, and the same problems people have.

engineers.title: Observability
engineers.summary: Traces are the only record of what an agent actually did, and the loop that turns them into a better agent.

everyone.title: Observability
everyone.summary: You cannot know what an agent did by reading its code. A trace is the record of every step, and the loop that uses it to improve the agent.

engineers.title: Prompt Engineering
engineers.summary: Writing the input that makes the output you want the most likely one, and why the job title disappeared.

everyone.title: Prompt Engineering
everyone.summary: How to write what you ask an AI so that you get what you meant: two templates, examples, structure, thinking out loud, and roles.

engineers.title: Context Engineering
engineers.summary: Deciding what earns a place in a limited context window, and why more context makes answers worse.

everyone.title: Context Engineering
everyone.summary: Why a long chat makes the AI worse, and the techniques that decide what goes into the chat and what stays out.

engineers.title: Code Agents
engineers.summary: Why an agent that can write and run code can do almost anything, and the eight standard ways you extend one.

everyone.title: Code Agents
everyone.summary: A coding agent can build what you describe, even if you cannot code. Why code is the skill that replaces the others, and the standard parts every coding agent has.

engineers.title: Agents in Practice
engineers.summary: Four free courses from Claude Academy that take you from reading about agents to using them every day.

everyone.title: Agents in Practice
everyone.summary: Three free courses that teach you to work with an AI agent, by doing the work yourself.

engineers.title: Harness Engineering
engineers.summary: The mechanical scaffolding around a model that keeps a non-deterministic agent on track, and why the same model scores differently in different harnesses.

everyone.title: Harness Engineering
everyone.summary: Asking an AI nicely gets you a good success rate, never a guarantee. The harness is the surroundings that make some rules impossible to break.

engineers.title: Loop Engineering
engineers.summary: Designing the loop that keeps an agent working until a goal is met, and what happens when nobody is left to press enter.

everyone.title: Loop Engineering
everyone.summary: People used to sit over their agents and press enter. Loop engineering lets a script or another agent keep the work going for hours or days.

engineers.title: Agentic UI
engineers.summary: How an agent's work reaches the screen while it is still running, and AG-UI, the protocol that lets any front end talk to any agent.

everyone.title: Agentic UI
everyone.summary: How an AI agent shows its work on the screen while it is still working, and AG-UI, the shared language that lets any screen talk to any agent.

engineers.title: Security
engineers.summary: How people get models to produce what they should not, and the guardrails, guard models and red-teaming tools used to stop them.

everyone.title: Security
everyone.summary: How people trick AI systems, including hidden instructions inside documents, and the guards that stop them.

engineers.title: Personal Agents
engineers.summary: Agents that live with you rather than in a repository: lifelong memory, self-written skills, and reachable from the chat apps you already use.

everyone.title: Personal Agents
everyone.summary: An AI agent pointed at your life: always on, reached on WhatsApp, remembering you. The story behind it, the big companies' versions, and the risks.

engineers.title: Agent Frameworks
engineers.summary: What an agent framework actually gives you, the three layers of the LangChain stack, and when a workflow tool is the better answer.

everyone.title: Agent Frameworks
everyone.summary: The names you will hear when a company builds an agent, what each is for, and when a fixed workflow beats an agent.

engineers.title: Inference Providers
engineers.summary: Who runs the model for you: the gateway, the first-party vendors, and what actually differs between them once you are paying.

everyone.title: Inference Providers
everyone.summary: Who rents you an AI model, the two ways to buy that access, and a buyer's checklist that goes beyond the price.

engineers.title: Inference Engines
engineers.summary: The software that actually runs the weights, when you should care, and what changes once you are serving more than yourself.

everyone.title: Inference Engines
everyone.summary: The software that actually runs a model, and the three reasons a company would run it on its own computers.

engineers.title: UI Design
engineers.summary: Getting an interface out of a model, and the one file that stops every generated screen looking like a different product.

everyone.title: UI Design
everyone.summary: AI can design a screen from a description, but every screen comes out different. Brand rules in a file fix that, and a person still has to check the parts you cannot see.
